method.label: Count the choices for the power of two

annotationRationale: The factorial valuation gives exponent eighteen. Unique divisor exponent choices produce nineteen equally sized groups, and classical probability compares the odd group with all groups.
sourceMethod: Followed the official power-of-two valuation and divisor-grouping argument, explaining why the representation is unique and why the unknown odd-divisor count cancels.

review.mathCheck: The exponent of 2 is 10+5+2+1=18. For every odd divisor b of the odd part, the divisors 2^i b have exactly 19 possibilities, including both endpoints i=0 and i=18. Exactly one is odd, giving 1/19, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA solution 16, page 6: count powers of 2 and group divisors by their odd parts. The optional complete factorization is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: All three immediate concepts fit. Divisor counting and classical probability are assessed; factorial valuation supplies the supporting exponent calculation.
